note: Feature on five Ukrainian athletes who joined the defence forces; Amosov gets one full section (territorial defence, fighting for Irpin, lost comrades, one quoted post, UFC debut Dec 2025). Centrality: a full section among five people, could be only_mentioned. Source/act: the section is the writer's retelling with one old quote of his, so media/gives_news_of_him, but himself/speaks_of_himself is defensible. Fact: his war service is life outside the cage but nothing here is new, so no_fact is defensible.

The whole piece is about Topuria's favourite restaurant in Spain (Nou Collonet on Tabarca), with a food influencer's negative visit. Act: nothing in the list fits a lifestyle profile exactly; gives_news_of_him (a fact about his life) is the nearest, none_of_these is defensible.

Hokit's tirade is aimed at Pereira; Topuria appears in two sentences of the quotes (neither he nor Pereira deserves a title shot next, make them earn it). Centrality: two sentences inside someone else's story, but they are directly about him, so one_of_several is defensible. Act: 'make him earn it' is steering, but it reads equally as an assessment (assesses_him).

Topuria's own essay for Marca, quoted at length: the promise he made himself as a child, his parents, six years apart from them, the 2008 war, arriving in Spain. Childhood and family, in his own words.

Makhachev on DJ's podcast: Topuria is young, hopes he returns, if he focuses he can be champion again; then a section where his physical trainer Jesús Gallo says his recovery is remarkably fast and he is working to return next year, so 2026 is ruled out. Source: Makhachev leads the article (other_fighter; the text says Topuria asked for that fight but it is pending, so not opponent_side), but the only new fact comes from his_team. Act: assessment vs advice (steers_him). Fact: health (recovery update) vs next_fight (return in 2027). Next fight: 'not in 2026, next year' is a timeline but vague. He_speaks: his post-fight remark about underestimating Gaethje is paraphrased, no direct quote.

Donchenko is the speaker throughout, but he talks about Makhachev's streak vs Silva's, Garry's mindset and Amosov as the man to test the champion, not about himself; his Soriano win is one clause of background. The guide puts 'him talking about another fighter, even at length' under only_mentioned, though he is the article's voice, hence unsure. Act none_of_these: he assesses other fighters, nobody does anything regarding him.

Long interview with manager Vladyslav Soroka about Ukrainian MMA, KSW, Yakymenko and who might reach the UFC; Amosov is one clause in the lead ('is in the UFC rankings'). Source none_of_these: the speaker is a manager of other fighters, not his; act none_of_these: nobody does anything regarding him.

Sport.ua 'watch live' preview of Donchenko vs Soriano at UFC Paris: records, his three-fight streak, main event, start times, broadcaster. Centrality: a preview of a fight of his covering both fighters per the guide, though Soriano gets one sentence, so main_subject is defensible. Fact: card position and start times (fight_week_event) vs the bout itself (next_fight). Result: a stray line 'the Ukrainian won his fourth in a row' sits among the page's teaser links after the article body; I treated it as page furniture from a later update.

Malki Kawa posts a 'Rematch' graphic with 'we want this fight': a demand for an immediate Gaethje rematch; the article adds that Gaethje has closed the door, the UFC may prefer Pimblett, his return will not come before 2027 (realistically March-June), and that the swelling has gone down and he is back in Miami. Fact/firmness: the main news is a wish, which the guide sends to no_fact, but the article also gives a return window and a recovery update, so next_fight/wish is my pick with no_fact/none as the alternative. Next fight: the rematch is a wish (no), but the 2027 return window is a timeline (yes), though it is the outlet's estimate.

Announcement of speakers at a sports forum in León; Topuria appears only to identify Dr Aldo Martínez as his performance director. Source: nothing new about him, so answered for the main content, a speaker line-up announced with nobody quoted (no_one); none_of_these (the forum organisers) is defensible. Act none_of_these: nobody does anything regarding him.

Kawa replies to Abdelaziz's claim that Usman Nurmagomedov would make Topuria quit: Topuria would beat the whole roster including Gaethje, still No. 1, 'when the comeback comes you will see'. Opinion and defence only, no date or opponent.

Weigh-in report: Donchenko and Soriano both made 77.11 kg; fight is 5 September in Paris, start times, broadcaster, his third bout of the year after beating Berggren in Baku. Centrality: a weigh-in covering both fighters, but the body is mostly about him, so main_subject is defensible. Next fight: opponent and date are stated, but as fight-week routine rather than as news of a booking.

Topuria's message to Georgian fans in a TBC spot: he will come back stronger, his greatest wins are ahead. The article recaps his injuries (two orbital fractures, septum, and a foot fracture he admitted in his essay) and mentions echoes of a Gaethje rematch and rumours of Pimblett. Fact: the message is talk, but the foot fracture could be read as health news. Next fight: rematch echo and Pimblett rumour are too vague for me to count as talks. Health: injuries recalled as background rather than an update.

A near-content-free 112.ua piece citing Sport.ua: Donchenko took part in the Paris event and showed his skills at the weigh-in, in the octagon and at the press conference; no result, no opponent named. Source/act: an event with nobody speaking, but the piece is mostly the writer's puffery, so media/gives_news_of_him is defensible. Fact: weigh-in and presser are fight-week routine, but 'in the octagon' implies the fight without reporting it, so none_of_these (he took part) is defensible.

Pimblett calls Topuria out after beating BSD ('I'm gonna absolutely rinse their lives'); Topuria replies 'Spaniards don't get knocked out either, be careful what you wish for'. Pimblett calling him out does not make it one_of_several. No return date, UFC has no plans; injuries recalled as background.

Aspinall vacates the heavyweight title in his own words; Donchenko does not appear anywhere in the text (the only watchlist name is Amosov, in a 'read also' link). Source answered for the main content (Aspinall speaking); act none_of_these because he is absent.

Analyst Álvaro Colmenero says Topuria will return to public life in September after three months away: July for recovering and treatments, August for holidays. Fact none_of_these: a return to public view is not a listed kind; personal_life is the nearest alternative. Health: 'July was for recovering from his injuries and treatments' is a thin update on how he is; I read it as background.

Gaethje says his hands are still hurt and he will not return until 2027; the lightweight queue (Tsarukyan, Oliveira, Holloway) follows. Topuria is named only as the opponent in the fight where the injuries happened. Centrality: the guide's 'another fighter's news tied to a fight already fought' clause could make it one_of_several, but the fight is not discussed, only referenced. Act none_of_these: Gaethje speaks about himself, nothing regarding Topuria.
UFC Paris results page; Donchenko's bout is one line: def. Soriano via unanimous decision (30-27 x2, 29-28).

Pimblett on his own next fight (December if all goes to plan, no opponent yet); asked about Topuria he would love it but 'nothing yet, no one's spoke to me'. Centrality: one paragraph on a wished-for fight, which the guide says does not count for one_of_several. Source: Pimblett is publicly linked to a Topuria fight only by his own wish, so other_fighter rather than opponent_side. Act: a mild callout; gives_news_of_him (no talks have happened) is defensible. Fact: 'no conversations' is the absence of talks, so no_fact rather than next_fight.
